plan.what: State compression at a large budget: 5,902 bits per card, 3,028 per note (asked by outside research; int8 is 26,624 / 14,336), codebooks fitted on the best model’s own states, scored after training on the best model (SM36)
plan.decides: Nearly free, but not cheaper than the int formats in practice: +0.00009 curve / +0.00015 instant (+0.77% / +0.70% vs the big model, 458 users), state 15.3 MB vs 37.6 MB for the smallest int format, but ~30 MB of codebooks to ship and ~11× slower scoring (5,005 vs ~56k reviews/s)

plan.decides: Nearly free: 16-bit scales and int8 short-term vectors cost nothing (±0.00000); the smallest format (11,824 / 10,272 bits, 37.6 MB, −46% vs int8) costs only the int4-card +0.00005 / +0.00005 already known from SM45

plan.what: Faster held-out scoring: benchmark metrics computed on arrays instead of Python loops (same results bit for bit), and scoring 2 or 4 users at once on the GPU

backlog.item: Benchmark labels for the 1,493 training users of the 2,225-user set
backlog.why: The label database only covers validation and test users; the 2,225 set scored nothing (10-19)

backlog.item: Training with carried state between a user’s windows
backlog.why: Moved up 10-18 (user): full-history context at short-window speed (2,048 windows ~5x faster than 32k). Designed, CPU prototype exact; code started 10-18

backlog.item: Instant-weighted (x2) final decay (fixed and checked, ready to run)
backlog.why: Moved back 10-18: instant already passes the bar (+0.94%) and the weighting likely costs curve, the failing head. Insurance if a later model slips on instant. Only if SM50 shows head slack

backlog.item: Teacher targets from the big model’s full-history replay
backlog.why: Needed with carried state; 5.2 h GPU, 3.7 GB. Already in use: the SM40v2 / SM36 final decays train on replay targets (5k users); 8k needs them for the 3,000 extra users (part of SM55)

backlog.item: State compression (~400 bits per card/note) with codebooks learned during training, in the one-epoch 32k decay of the best model
backlog.why: Done 10-20: learned codebooks during the one-epoch 32k decay (outside research’s method) only cut the compression cost from +0.42% / +0.93% to +0.38% / +0.79% (68 users) vs int8 state. Not enough for the ≤ +1.0% bar on top of the best model; int8 state stays the standard. Payoff would have been ~45× smaller state (4.6 KB → ~0.1 KB per card)

backlog.item: State compression trained in (QAT) at ~400/400 bits per card/note, during the final decay only
backlog.why: Done 10-18, re-checked 10-19 on 68 users: worse than compressing after training (+0.0014 [+0.0005, +0.0023] curve / +0.0010 [+0.0007, +0.0013] instant; frozen k-means codebooks, 0.25-epoch decay). The new 34 users agree with the first 34, so it is the method, not the sample: the short decay with frozen books makes the model itself worse (uncompressed +1.8% / +2.3%)

backlog.item: Muon optimizer for the student
backlog.why: Done 10-20: Muon for the one-epoch 32k decay ties the best model on curve and is a little better on instant (-0.00018, about -0.05 points; 464 users: +0.81% / +0.68% vs the big model). Kept as the new best; outside research also tunes its learning rate (open tuning queue)

backlog.item: Label-free reference: the big model fine-tuned with review type switched off
backlog.why: Honest best a big model can do without review type. Fine-tune first: a cheap from-scratch big-model-size retrain lost +0.0037 / +0.0043 in outside runs

backlog.item: Deployment-realistic scoring without the duration leak
backlog.why: Intervals as Anki knows them when it shows the card; both models, cheap. Outside runs: +0.0002 / +0.0004 cost. Week plan: Sun 10-25

backlog.why: w64 still ~21% slower than the w32 fast kernels at short windows; bit-for-bit identical

backlog.why: Timing test first, then a learning-rate check

backlog.why: Card prior reviews, FSRS state, user pass rate; modest prior

backlog.item: Review-number flags as inputs
backlog.why: Measured 10-18: curve +0.00003, instant −0.00004 vs the same run without them (464 users)

backlog.item: Data diversity vs epochs: many users few epochs (10+1 epochs) vs 10× fewer users 10× more epochs (100+10), same number of gradient steps, both scored on the 732-user set
backlog.why: User idea 10-19, not urgent. Does the small model gain more from more users or from more passes? Full size (5k users × 11 epochs) would take ~10.5 h per arm, so scaled to fit 5–6 h: 1,250 users × (10+1) vs 125 users × (100+10), the fast 2,048-window KD recipe (~108k reviews/s), equal reviews seen. Slot: 10-20 after SM32c

backlog.item: Measure first: the repeat stress test and a “mature card, then rapid repeats” slice, on the best small model (SM36) and the big model
backlog.why: From an outside audit of SM40 (10-20): the curve is trained only at the next real review, so its long-term tail can change freely between answers; repeated rapid Goods on a mature card make the interval jump, then collapse (the big model jumps too). CPU only. Tells whether it matters on real histories or only in the stress test

backlog.item: Consistency on real rapid Good pairs: compare the curve before and after the second Good at the same future dates (days, months, a year)
backlog.why: Our simpler first version of ST01: ~5–6M real pairs in the training data, both curves already computed in the same pass, so almost no extra cost; a small penalty, only for short gaps where Good was expected. One-epoch decay like SM42, judged on 732 users (curve and instant must not get worse) plus the stress test

backlog.item: Consistency on made-up rapid Good sequences from real card histories (the audit’s first proposal)
backlog.why: Only if ST01a is not enough: inserted reviews also change what the deck, note and user memories see, so it is costly to build in our training

backlog.item: Separate short-term and long-term updates (a learned gate on the long-term curve)
backlog.why: Architecture change; only if consistency losses fail the quality gate

backlog.item: Smaller int state round 2 + lossless compression of the stored codes
backlog.why: See the week plan; no retraining

backlog.item: Head-only fine-tunes (trunk frozen), one per head
backlog.why: Cheapest head-specific test; state unchanged

backlog.item: Checkpoint (weight) averaging over the final decay
backlog.why: Needs snapshots: saved during the next decay (SM39 arm 1)

backlog.item: Stacked decay of the week’s winners, then 2,225-user check
backlog.why: End of week 10-26/27

backlog.item: Per-head distillation weight (more teacher on one head, more real answers on the other)
backlog.why: Cheap to add to a decay; small expected gain

backlog.item: Train on more users than the 5,000 used so far (SM43: more users win)
backlog.why: First count how many benchmark users are not used for training or evaluation (CPU, minutes)

backlog.item: Runbooks skip the users that never fit in GPU memory instead of retrying them 3×
backlog.why: ~35 min of GPU lost on 10-21 (SM44, SM46); no GPU needed

backlog.item: Full retrain from scratch with carried state at 2,048 windows (every epoch, not just the decay), on 8k users if SM55 wins
backlog.why: Never tested: SM42 showed 2 late carried epochs add nothing before the decay, so the gain may be small. ~22 h GPU on 8k users (~15 h on 5k). Decide after SM55 (user, 10-21)

backlog.item: Instant-only small model: retrain from scratch with only the instant head, against a matched joint baseline (same users, seeds, epochs); record training time, reviews/s, GPU memory and instant LogLoss on 723 users
backlog.why: Goal: better instant predictions, not less space. Does giving all of the model to instant beat sharing it with the curve, or does the curve task help instant learn? Many people mostly use instant; a second, curve-only model could cover the rest (both = double the state). No rush: later this week if a slot opens, else next week (user, 10-21)

backlog.item: UM+ small vs big model with each model’s slope, in the Search Stats Extended conventions (5-point disagreement bins, bins under 200 reviews hidden for slopes but counted in UM+). The slope closer to 0 is the more right model; the two slopes always differ by exactly 1, so a tie is +0.5 for the small model (and so −0.5 for the small model would mean a tieminus;0.5 for the big model). Curve and instant, SM36 (and SM55 if it wins), 723 users and the own collection (aggregate only)
backlog.why: LogLoss says how far the small model is behind, not where. Reference: the user’s chart on the own collection, instant, big (legacy) +0.425 vs SM40 −0.575 (UM+ 0.0155 vs 0.0180). Thu 10-22 after SM55: ~1 h GPU to save both models’ predictions, the rest on the CPU

backlog.item: Better distillation, step 2: also learn the big model’s whole forgetting curve (its predictions at fixed intervals, e.g. 1 d / 7 d / 30 d / 180 d), not one point per review
backlog.why: Only if step 1 shows a gain (user, 10-22). Needs new code and a new export of the big model’s predictions (GPU, a few hours, +~16 B per review). Step 3 (copy the big model’s internal state) only if 1–2 show the small model can’t follow

results.name: State compression at a large budget: 5,902 bits per card, 3,028 per note (codebooks fitted after training on the best model’s own states, no retraining), best model (SM36), w8 weights
results.fork: SM36 int8 state: 0.29804 / 0.27397 (+0.74% / +0.64% vs the big model)
results.takeaway: Nearly free at 4.5× smaller than int8: +0.00009 [+0.00006, +0.00012] curve / +0.00015 [+0.00012, +0.00018] instant. 15.3 MB of state for 13,973 cards / 13,198 notes (int8 70.2 MB, smallest int format 37.6 MB at +0.00004 / +0.00005), but the codebooks add ~30 MB and scoring is ~11× slower (5,005 reviews/s on the GPU). Only the 464 set: all 732 users would take ~4 h

results.name: Compressed card/note state at ~400 and ~800 bits (codebooks), scored on the GPU: SM42 model with codebooks fitted after training, and SM32c with codebooks learned in training
results.fork: same model, int8 state: 0.30155 / 0.27777 (+0.71% / +0.70% vs the big model)
results.takeaway: ~800 bits is not free (row shown): +0.37% curve / +0.67% instant over int8, so +1.08% / +1.38% vs the big model, over the +1.0% bar. ~400 bits: +1.43% / +1.88%. Learned codebooks (SM32c) at ~400 bits: +1.35% / +1.71%; they help that model, but its int8 starts worse (+1.92% / +2.21%). GPU scorer: int8 92k, ~400 bits 47k, ~800 bits 14k reviews/s of model time. Same on 458 users (464 set)

results.name: Faster held-out scoring: benchmark metrics on arrays instead of Python loops, and 2 or 4 users at once on the GPU (timing run, 40 users of the 732 set, SM36 int8 + int4-card state)
results.eval: 40 users, 4.51M review-evals per run, 2 runs per arm
results.takeaway: 1.56× faster pool scoring, same numbers bit for bit: array metrics 61,430 reviews/s (1.33×), 2 users at once 66,484 (1.44×), 4 at once 72,074 (1.56×). Two state formats on the 732 set: ~36 min → ~23 min. GPU memory 13.1 → 14.5 GB with several users at once

results.name: Smallest int state without retraining: int4 cards + int8 notes + 16-bit row scales + int8 short-term vectors (11,824 / 10,272 bits per card / note, 37.6 MB for 13,973 cards / 13,198 notes), best model (SM36), w8 weights
results.takeaway: −46% state size for +0.00005: 16-bit scales and int8 short-term vectors are free (±0.00000 alone, together, and on top of int4 cards); the only cost is the int4 cards (+0.00005 [+0.00003, +0.00006] curve / +0.00005 [+0.00004, +0.00006] instant). Without int4 cards: 51.9 MB (−26%) at zero cost. Same on 458 users (464 set): +0.76% / +0.66%

results.name: Data diversity vs epochs, full size: 125 users × (100 + 10 decay) epochs vs 1,250 users × (10 + 1 decay), same ~1.06B reviews seen, from scratch, 2,048 windows
results.fork: 1,250 users × 11 epochs: 0.30863 / 0.28462 (+2.40% / +2.43% vs the big model)
results.takeaway: More users win, and the gap grows with training: fewer users, more passes +0.77% [+0.58, +1.00] curve / +0.55% [+0.47, +0.65] instant (mini: +0.36% / +0.46%). Worse in every size band (light / mid / heavy +0.97 / +0.76 / +0.76% curve). Keep training on as many users as possible

results.name: Data diversity vs epochs, mini: 100 users × 10 epochs vs 1,000 users × 1 epoch (same 73.5M reviews seen, from scratch, 2,048 windows, constant LR)
results.fork: 1,000 users × 1 epoch: 0.32774 / 0.30309 (+8.74% / +9.08% vs the big model)
results.takeaway: More users win, mostly on instant: fewer users, more passes +0.36% [−0.06, +0.82] curve / +0.46% [+0.25, +0.69] instant; calibration worse too (RMSE(bins) 0.0687 vs 0.0642). By history length the loss is all on heavy users (+0.53% / +0.64%); light users gain slightly (−0.25% / −0.41%). Both arms are early in training (+9% vs the big model); the full-size run tells whether this holds

results.name: Control: the best model’s one-epoch 32k decay (carry on), from the plain 32k epoch 10 (no carried-state epochs before it)
results.takeaway: Ties the best. vs best −0.00000 [−0.00014, +0.00014] / +0.00004 [+0.00001, +0.00007] (464 users). The 2 epochs with carried state before the decay add nothing; the gain is the one-epoch 32k decay with carry itself (vs dec10 −0.00091 / −0.00051). Simpler recipe: plain 32k training, then that decay

results.name: Pruning: 7-layer cut (2+1+1 layers in the deck / preset / user streams, 204,782 params, −38%), fine-tuned, then the best model’s one-epoch 32k decay
results.fork: big model 0.29632 / 0.27281 on the same users; best (SM40) 0.29843 / 0.27469
results.takeaway: Fails. vs the best +0.36% [+0.16, +0.54] / +0.42% [+0.37, +0.46] (limit +0.25%); on 724 users +0.44% / +0.43% (+1.10% / +1.11% vs the big model). The cut streams carry real signal; the 331k model stays the smallest that meets the bar

results.name: State compression (~400 bits per card/note): trained in vs applied after training, re-checked on 34 more users
results.fork: Δ% = trained-in vs after-training compression, paired
results.takeaway: Same answer on the new 34 users (+0.0015 / +0.0010) as on the first 34 (+0.0012 / +0.0010). All 68: +0.0014 [+0.0005, +0.0023] / +0.0010 [+0.0007, +0.0013]. After-training compression costs +0.37% / +0.86% vs uncompressed. Not a sample-size issue: the short decay with frozen codebooks hurts. Next try: codebooks learned in the full decay (SM32c)

results.name: One-epoch 32k decay of carried state v2 (SM40) on your collection
results.takeaway: Nearly level with the big model on curve. Calibration RMSE(bins) 0.0256 / 0.0209 (dec10 0.0286 / 0.0207, big model 0.0224 / 0.0200)

results.eval: 458 users (6 longest do not fit in memory with dumps)
results.takeaway: Spaced reviews (71%): +0.60% / +0.61% (dec10 +0.85% / +0.79%). Same-day (27%): +1.07% / +0.91% (dec10 +1.22% / +1.10%). The remaining curve gap is mostly learning steps

results.label: s-w64kd-gate-ctx32768c-dec10/w8+s8 (732 pool)

results.name: Carried state v2 (strided lanes, exact state): 2 epochs at 2,048 from epoch 10 + decay at 2,048, full-history targets
results.takeaway: Best 2,048-window model by far: −0.0009 / −0.0013 vs no carry, −0.0009 / −0.0011 vs v1. Before decay it beats 32k e10 (−0.0002 / −0.0011); after decay it trails 32k dec10 by +0.0003 [−0.0001, +0.0007] / +0.0004: the 2,048 decay gains less than the 32k one. Next: decay v2 at 32k
results.label: s-w64kd-gate-sc-lanes-dec12/w8+s8

results.name: Carried state v1, arm B (control, no carry): 2 epochs at 2,048 from epoch 10 + decay, full-history targets
results.takeaway: Gate users at e12: carry beat it by −0.0013 / −0.0005 (CIs below zero); on 464 users after decay only the instant gain holds (−0.0002)

results.name: Carried state v1, arm A (carry): 2 epochs at 2,048 from epoch 10 + decay, full-history targets
results.takeaway: Paired with arm B (same recipe, no carry), 464 users: −0.00001 / −0.00020 after decay [curve CI −0.0003, +0.0003; instant −0.00033, −0.00007]; before decay (e12) −0.00056 / −0.00041. The decay erased most of the curve gain. Both 2,048-window arms stay behind 32k (+0.0012 / +0.0015). v2 (exact state) is running
results.label: s-w64kd-gate-sc-carry-dec12/w8+s8

results.name: After-training compression of dec10 with codebooks fitted on dec10’s own states
results.fork: big model 0.32132 / 0.28497; dec10 uncompressed 0.32194 / 0.28716; original codebooks 0.32314 / 0.28946
results.takeaway: Same cost as the codebooks from the earlier model (+0.00127 / +0.00231 vs +0.00120 / +0.00231). The cost is the bit budget, not the codebook fit
results.label: dec10/w8+vq378x412 (dec10 books)

results.name: State compression (~400/400 bits per card/note) trained into the final decay, scored compressed
results.fork: big model 0.32132 / 0.28497 on the same users; compressed after training (dec10) 0.32314 / 0.28946; uncompressed dec10 0.32194 / 0.28716
results.takeaway: Worse than compressing after training (+0.0012 / +0.0010). Not a codec mismatch, not stale codebooks (refitting them on the new model’s states: 0.32799 / 0.29382, worse still; it learned around the frozen books). Training with the compression in the loop hurts here; dropped for now
results.label: qat/w8+vq378x412

results.name: Review-number flags as inputs (2nd / 3rd / 4th+ review), 2 epochs at 2,048 + decay
results.fork: big model 0.29766 / 0.27216; same run without flags 0.30259 / 0.27667
results.takeaway: No gain: curve +0.00003 [−0.00005, +0.00012], instant −0.00004 [−0.00006, −0.00003] (233 / 256 of 464 users better). Instant gain real but ~1/10 of what would matter. Dropped; at 32k the model can count reviews itself anyway

results.name: One-epoch final decay at 2,048 windows (vs our quarter epoch)
results.fork: big model 0.29766 / 0.27216; same start with a quarter-epoch decay 0.30259 / 0.27668
results.takeaway: Longer decay helps: −0.00033 curve [−0.00068, −0.00008] / −0.00019 instant [−0.00025, −0.00012] (292 / 351 of 464 users better). Smaller than the gain seen in outside runs; a 1-epoch decay at 32k would cost ~4½ h

results.name: Speed check of the compression-in-training GPU kernels
results.fork: seconds per update: plain 1.12, with compression 1.38 (fused kernels), 3.4–3.8 (PyTorch loop)
results.takeaway: Worse than compressing after training (+0.0012 / +0.0010). Not a codec mismatch, not stale codebooks (refitting them on the new model’s states: 0.32799 / 0.29382, worse still; it learned around the frozen books). Training with the compression in the loop hurts here; dropped for now

results.name: Training speed profile (quiet GPU): student at 2,048 / 8,192 / 16,384 / 32,768 windows and the big-model-size model
